name: 15e minhash shingles
title: Matching minimum hashes estimate how much two documents overlap
subtitle: Word shingles of length 3; four hash functions give each shingle a random number from 0 to 99

steps.caption: Each sentence is cut into runs of three consecutive words, called shingles. The two sentences differ in one word, yet that word sits inside 3 of the 6 shingles of each, so they share only 3 of 9 distinct shingles and J = 0.333.

Hash function h1 gives every shingle a random number. Each document keeps its smallest number (bold orange): A keeps 7 and B keeps 10, so they differ. They match only when the smallest number in the union belongs to a shared shingle, which happens with probability J.

Hash function h2 gives every shingle a random number. Each document keeps its smallest number (bold orange): A keeps 22 and B keeps 22, so they match. They match only when the smallest number in the union belongs to a shared shingle, which happens with probability J.

Hash function h3 gives every shingle a random number. Each document keeps its smallest number (bold orange): A keeps 7 and B keeps 19, so they differ. They match only when the smallest number in the union belongs to a shared shingle, which happens with probability J.

Hash function h4 gives every shingle a random number. Each document keeps its smallest number (bold orange): A keeps 8 and B keeps 8, so they match. They match only when the smallest number in the union belongs to a shared shingle, which happens with probability J.

With k = 4 the estimate is 0.50 against a true 0.333, which is noisy. The spread of the estimate is the square root of J(1 - J)/k, so 128 hash functions bring it to about 0.04 while each document is still stored as only 128 numbers.
